questions.question: In which epic is it mentioned that dying during Uttarayana leads to salvation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahabharata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mahabharata** is one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, and it explicitly describes the spiritual significance of **Uttarayana** through the narrative of **Bhishma Pitamaha**.
 
• **Bhishma**, the patriarch of the Kuru dynasty, possessed the rare boon of **Iccha Mrityu** (death at will), granted by his father, **King Shantanu**.
 
• After being mortally wounded during the **Kurukshetra War** by **Arjuna**, Bhishma chose to lie on a bed of arrows (**Sharashayya**) rather than giving up his life immediately.
 
• He intentionally delayed his departure from the mortal world for **58 days** to wait for the onset of **Uttarayana**, the period when the sun begins its northward journey.
 
• According to the epic, dying during this auspicious period allows the soul to travel through the **Devayana** (the path of gods), leading directly to **Salvation** or **Moksha** and liberation from the cycle of rebirth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uttarayana and its Significance:**

 
 
• It is the **six-month period** between the **Winter Solstice** and the **Summer Solstice**, characterized by the sun moving into the northern hemisphere.
 
• The festival of **Makar Sankranti** traditionally marks the beginning of this period in the Hindu solar calendar.
 
• In the **Bhagavad Gita**, which is a section of the **Mahabharata**, **Lord Krishna** confirms that those who depart the world during the light of the day and the six months of the northern sun attain the **Supreme Abode**.
 
 
 
• **Other Epics and Texts:**
 
 
• **Ramayana:** An epic chronicling the life of **Lord Rama**, but the theological focus on waiting for Uttarayana for salvation is specific to the legend of Bhishma in the Mahabharata.
 
• **Vedas:** The oldest scriptures of Hinduism containing hymns and rituals; while they discuss cosmic order (**Rta**), the specific narrative of Bhishma's death is found in the **Itihasa** (History) category.
 
• **Bhagavata Purana:** Focuses on **Bhakti** (devotion) and the incarnations of **Vishnu**, particularly **Krishna**, but is distinct from the primary historical account of the Kuru war.

questions.question: If a planet takes 88 Earth days to orbit the Sun, what is its orbital period in seconds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7.6 × 10⁶ s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **orbital period** is defined as the time a celestial object takes to complete one full revolution around another object; in this context, it refers to a planet orbiting the **Sun**.
 
• To determine the period in seconds, we must convert **88 Earth days** using standard units of time: 1 day consists of **24 hours**, 1 hour contains **60 minutes**, and 1 minute contains **60 seconds**.
 
• The total number of seconds in a single **solar day** is calculated by the product: 24 × 60 × 60 = **86,400 seconds**.
 
• By multiplying the given orbital duration of **88 days** by the number of seconds per day, we find: 88 × 86,400 = **7,603,200 seconds**.
 
• In **scientific notation**, this value is expressed as **7.6032 × 10⁶ s**. Rounding to two significant figures as per the provided options results in **7.6 × 10⁶ s**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mercury and Orbital Mechanics**

 
 
• **Mercury** is the planet characterized by an orbital period of approximately **88 Earth days** (specifically 87.97 days), making it the fastest planet in our **Solar System**.
 
• Because it is the closest planet to the Sun, it must maintain a high **orbital velocity** (averaging 47.36 km/s) to counteract the Sun's massive **gravitational pull**.
 
 
 
• **Kepler's Third Law**
 
 
• The relationship between a planet's distance from the Sun and its period is governed by **Kepler's Law of Periods**, which states that the square of the **orbital period** (T) is proportional to the cube of the **semi-major axis** (a) of its orbit (T² ∝ a³).
 
• This law implies that planets further from the Sun, such as **Jupiter** or **Neptune**, have significantly longer orbital periods compared to terrestrial planets like Earth or Mercury.

questions.question: Which planet is called the stormy planet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jupiter**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jupiter** is the largest planet in our **Solar System** and is primarily classified as a **gas giant** due to its composition of **hydrogen** and **helium**.
 
• It is widely known as the **stormy planet** because its atmosphere is in a constant state of turbulence, featuring high-velocity **zonal winds** and massive **vortices**.
 
• The most famous feature of Jupiter is the **Great Red Spot**, an enormous **anticyclonic storm** that is larger than **Earth** and has been raging for at least **350 years**.
 
• Because Jupiter lacks a solid rocky surface, there is no **friction** to slow down these atmospheric disturbances, allowing storms to persist for decades or even centuries.
 
• The planet also exhibits **White Ovals** and **Brown Barges**, which are smaller but equally intense storm systems within its distinct **cloud bands**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mercury**:

 
 
• It is the **closest planet** to the Sun and the smallest in the solar system.
 
• Mercury has a very thin **exosphere** instead of a traditional atmosphere, meaning it cannot generate **weather** or storms.
 
 
 
• **Mars**:
 
 
• Often called the **Red Planet** due to the prevalence of **iron oxide** on its surface.
 
• While it experiences massive **dust storms** that can occasionally cover the entire planet, its thin atmosphere lacks the complex gaseous dynamics found on **Jupiter**.
 
 
 
• **Venus**:
 
 
• Known as **Earths twin**, it has an extremely dense atmosphere of **carbon dioxide** and clouds of **sulfuric acid**.
 
• It is the **hottest planet** in the solar system due to a runaway **greenhouse effect**, rather than being defined primarily by storm activity.

questions.question: In which country was the 2nd BRIC Summit held in 2010?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brazil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **2nd BRIC Summit** was held on **April 15, 2010**, in the capital city of **Brasília**, **Brazil**.
 
• The summit was attended by the leaders of the four founding nations: **President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva** of Brazil, **President Dmitry Medvedev** of Russia, **Prime Minister Manmohan Singh** of India, and **President Hu Jintao** of China.
 
• The primary focus of this summit was the recovery from the **2008 global financial crisis** and the necessity of reforming international financial institutions like the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** and the **World Bank** to provide more voting power to emerging economies.
 
• A significant outcome of the 2010 meeting was the discussion regarding the expansion of the group, which eventually led to **South Africa** being invited to join the bloc by the end of that year.
 
• The leaders signed several agreements regarding **technical cooperation** and cooperation between their respective **development banks** to facilitate trade and investment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chronology of Early Summits**:

 
 
• **1st BRIC Summit**: Held in **Yekaterinburg**, **Russia**, on **June 16, 2009**. It was the first formal meeting of the group.
 
• **3rd BRICS Summit**: Held in **Sanya**, **China**, in **2011**. This was the first summit where **South Africa** participated as a full member, changing the acronym to **BRICS**.
 
• **4th BRICS Summit**: Hosted by **India** in **New Delhi** on **March 29, 2012**.
 
 
 
• **BRICS Concept and Expansion**:
 
 
• The acronym **BRIC** was originally coined by **Jim O'Neill** of **Goldman Sachs** in **2001** to highlight the economic potential of these four nations.
 
• In **August 2023**, during the **15th BRICS Summit** in **South Africa**, the group announced a major expansion, inviting countries including **Egypt**, **Ethiopia**, **Iran**, and the **United Arab Emirates** to join starting **January 1, 2024**.

questions.question: What is the theme of India's 79th Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Naya Bharat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **79th Independence Day** of India, to be celebrated on **August 15, 2025**, marks a significant milestone in the country's journey toward its centenary of freedom in 2047.
 
• The theme **Naya Bharat** (New India) reflects the government's commitment to building a nation that is self-reliant, technologically advanced, and inclusive of all social strata.
 
• The celebrations held at the historic **Red Fort** (Lal Qila) in **New Delhi** traditionally feature the unfurling of the **National Flag** by the **Prime Minister**, followed by a speech outlining the national roadmap.
 
• The theme emphasizes the vision of **Amrit Kaal**, focusing on the **Panch Pran** (Five Vows) which include the goal of a developed India, removing any trace of colonial mindset, taking pride in roots, unity, and sense of duty among citizens.
 
• **Naya Bharat** serves as an umbrella concept for various flagship schemes like **Digital India**, **Make in India**, and **PM Gati Shakti**, aiming to position India as a global powerhouse in the 21st century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Viksit Bharat @ 2047**:

 
 
• This is the overarching vision to transform India into a **Developed Nation** by its 100th year of independence.
 
• Key pillars include **economic growth**, **social progress**, **environmental sustainability**, and **good governance**.
 
 
 
• **The Red Fort's Historical Role**:
 
 
• Built by **Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan**, it has been the site for Independence Day addresses since **Jawaharlal Nehru** first hoisted the flag here in 1947.
 
• It is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** representing the architectural fusion of Persian, Timurid, and Indian styles.
 
 
 
• **Atmanirbhar Bharat**:
 
 
• A core component of the **Naya Bharat** theme, focusing on making India a global manufacturing hub and reducing import dependency.
 
• It highlights advancements in sectors like **Defense**, **Space**, and **Semiconductors**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a major source of water vapor in the air?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Evaporation from oceans**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Water vapor** is the gaseous state of water and serves as the primary greenhouse gas, responsible for maintaining the Earth's temperature through the **Hydrological Cycle**.
 
• The **Oceans** are the largest reservoirs of liquid water on the planet, covering approximately **71 percent** of the Earth's total surface area.
 
• Due to the massive surface area and the absorption of **Solar Radiation**, approximately **85 percent to 90 percent** of all atmospheric water vapor originates from the evaporation of seawater.
 
• **Evaporation** occurs when thermal energy increases the kinetic energy of water molecules, allowing them to overcome surface tension and escape into the air as a gas.
 
• The rate of this process is governed by **Surface Temperature**, **Wind Speed**, and the **Vapor Pressure Gradient** between the ocean surface and the lower atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transpiration**:

 
 
• This is the biological process where plants release water vapor through **Stomata**. When combined with land evaporation (**Evapotranspiration**), it accounts for the remaining **10 percent** of atmospheric moisture.
 
 
 
• **Combustion**:
 
 
• The chemical reaction of **Hydrocarbons** with oxygen produces **Carbon Dioxide** and water vapor. While significant in urban microclimates, it is a negligible contributor to global water vapor levels.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis**:
 
 
• This is the process by which green plants use **Sunlight** to convert water and carbon dioxide into **Glucose**. It acts as a consumer of water rather than a primary source of atmospheric vapor.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Smoke**:
 
 
• Emissions from factories often contain **Steam** and particulate matter. However, these **Anthropogenic** sources are localized and do not compare to the scale of natural oceanic evaporation.

questions.question: Which visionary is dubbed the 'father of fiber optics'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narinder Singh Kapany**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Narinder Singh Kapany** was an **Indian-American physicist** who is widely recognized globally as the **father of fiber optics** for his pioneering research in the **1950s**.
 
• In **1953**, while working at **Imperial College London**, he successfully demonstrated that light can be transmitted through a **bundle of glass fibers**, overcoming the traditional challenge of light leaking out of the sides.
 
• He achieved this by using a **cladding** material with a lower **refractive index**, which enabled **Total Internal Reflection**, the fundamental principle behind all modern optical communication.
 
• The term **fiber optics** was first coined by Kapany in a seminal article for **Scientific American** in **1960**, establishing the nomenclature for the entire industry.
 
• His work paved the way for a revolution in **telecommunications**, high-speed **broadband internet**, and medical applications like **endoscopy** and **laser-assisted surgery**.
 
• In recognition of his monumental contributions to **science and engineering**, the **Government of India** posthumously awarded him the **Padma Vibhushan**, the country's second-highest civilian honor, in **2021**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jay Chaudhry**:

 
 
• An **Indian-American billionaire** entrepreneur and the CEO of **Zscaler**, a leading company in **cloud security** and zero-trust architecture.
 
 
 
• **Vivek Sehgal**:
 
 
• The chairman and co-founder of **Motherson Group**, a major global player in the **automotive component** manufacturing industry.
 
 
 
• **Fiber Optic Cables**:
 
 
• These cables transmit data as **pulses of light** through strands of glass or plastic, offering significantly higher **bandwidth** and lower **attenuation** compared to traditional copper wires.
 
• This technology is the backbone of the **World Wide Web** and long-distance digital **data transmission**.

questions.question: The main river flowing through the Rajasthan desert is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Luni**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Luni River** is the only major river system in the **Thar Desert** (Great Indian Desert) and serves as the primary source of water for the arid regions of western **Rajasthan**.
 
• It originates in the **Pushkar Valley** of the **Aravalli Range**, near **Ajmer**, at an elevation of approximately **550 meters**, where it is initially known as the **Sagarmati**.

questions.question: Loktak Lake is located in which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Loktak Lake** is situated in the **Bishnupur district** of **Manipur** and is recognized as the largest **freshwater lake** in **North-East India**.
 
• The lake is globally renowned for its unique **phumdis**, which are floating islands composed of a heterogeneous mass of **vegetation**, **soil**, and **organic matter** in various stages of decomposition.
 
• It serves as a primary source for **hydropower generation**, **irrigation**, and **drinking water supply** in the region, while also supporting the livelihoods of local fishermen.
 
• The **Keibul Lamjao National Park**, located in the southeastern part of the lake, is the world’s only **floating national park** and is an integral part of the **Loktak ecosystem**.
 
• This ecosystem provides the sole natural habitat for the critically endangered **Sangai** (Rucervus eldii eldii), also known as the **dancing deer**, which is the **state animal** of **Manipur**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Conservation Status**:

 
 
• **Loktak Lake** was designated as a **wetland of international importance** under the **Ramsar Convention** on **March 23, 1990**.
 
• In 1993, it was listed under the **Montreux Record** due to ecological changes resulting from human activities and the construction of the **Ithai Barrage**.
 
 
 
• **Other Regional Lakes**:
 
 
• **Tripura**: Home to **Rudrasagar Lake**, a **Ramsar site** featuring the famous **Neermahal** water palace.
 
• **Assam**: Contains **Deepor Beel**, a permanent freshwater lake in the **Kamrup district** and a significant bird sanctuary.
 
• **Nagaland**: Known for **Shilloi Lake**, a natural foot-shaped lake located in the **Phek district**.

questions.question: In the Delhi Sultanate, ____ was one of the religious duties enjoined upon all Muslims.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zakat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Zakat** is defined as a mandatory **religious tax** and represents one of the **Five Pillars of Islam**, making it a compulsory duty for all eligible Muslims to support the needy.
 
• During the **Delhi Sultanate** (1206–1526), the administrative and fiscal systems were largely governed by the **Shariat** (Islamic Law), which identified **Zakat** as a specific tax on property and wealth.
 
• It was typically levied at a fixed rate of **2.5%** (or one-fortieth) on specific assets including **gold**, **silver**, **livestock**, and **merchandise** that had been in the owner's possession for at least one lunar year.
 
• The revenue generated from **Zakat** was strictly utilized for **charitable purposes**, such as providing for the **poor**, **widows**, **orphans**, and **religious institutions**, rather than for general state expenditures or military funding.
 
• It was distinct from other taxes like **Kharaj** (land tax) and **Jizya** because it was a purely religious obligation performed only by the Muslim subjects of the **Sultanate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mamluk**:

 
 
• Refers to the **Slave Dynasty** (1206–1290), the first ruling house of the **Delhi Sultanate** founded by **Qutub-ud-din Aibak**.
 
• The term **Mamluk** is an Arabic word for 'owned', signifying **slave-soldiers** of Turkish origin who rose to political power.
 
 
 
• **Ur**:
 
 
• This was a type of **village assembly** found specifically in the **Chola Empire** of South India, consisting of tax-paying residents.
 
• It operated alongside the **Sabha**, which was the assembly of **Brahmin** landholders in **Brahmadeya** villages.
 
 
 
• **Jizya and Khums**:
 
 
• **Jizya** was a protection tax levied on non-Muslim subjects (**Dhimmis**) in exchange for state protection and military exemption.
 
• **Khums** referred to the state's share of **war booty**, which was traditionally one-fifth of the total spoils captured during military campaigns.

questions.question: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation in ______ 2025 unveiled the National Cooperation Policy 2025 in New Delhi.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**January**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation **Amit Shah** officially unveiled the **National Cooperation Policy 2025** on **January 1, 2025**, during a ceremony held at **Bharat Mandapam**, New Delhi.
 
• The policy is designed to realize the vision of **Sahakar-se-Samriddhi** (Prosperity through Cooperation) by creating a more vibrant, transparent, and professional cooperative movement across the country.
 
• The draft of this policy was prepared by a **47-member National Level Committee** headed by former Union Minister **Suresh Prabhu**, which incorporated suggestions from various stakeholders, state governments, and national cooperative federations.
 
• The policy focuses on **10 major themes**, including strengthening the legal and institutional framework, enhancing financial sustainability, and promoting the use of **modern technology** and **digitalization** in cooperatives.
 
• It aims to increase the contribution of cooperatives to the national **GDP** and create a level playing field for them compared to other economic sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Cooperation**:

 
 
• Established by the Government of India in **July 2021** to provide a separate administrative, legal, and policy framework for the cooperative sector.
 
• It works to streamline processes for **Ease of Doing Business** for cooperatives and to enable the development of **Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS)**.
 
 
 
• **Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS)**:
 
 
• A major component of the new policy is the strengthening of approximately **63,000 functional PACS** by converting them into **Common Service Centres (CSCs)**.
 
• The computerization of PACS is a key project aimed at improving transparency and efficiency at the village level.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Framework**:
 
 
• The **97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011** added Part IXB to the Constitution, providing constitutional status and protection to cooperative societies.
 
• Promotion of cooperatives is also a **Directive Principle of State Policy** under **Article 43B**.

questions.question: Which state was ranked first for the month of July 2025 in the PM-JANMAN scheme?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **PM-JANMAN** (Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan) was launched on **November 15, 2023**, to coincide with **Janjatiya Gaurav Divas**, aiming to provide comprehensive development for **75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)**.
 
• For the ranking period of **July 2025**, **Gujarat** secured the **first rank** among all states by achieving the highest percentage of **saturation** in individual entitlement schemes, specifically in the issuance of **Aadhaar cards**, **caste certificates**, and **Jan Dhan bank accounts** for the PVTG population.
 
• The state demonstrated exceptional administrative efficiency by conducting intensive **Information, Education, and Communication (IEC)** campaigns and **saturation camps** across districts such as **Narmada**, **Tapi**, and **Dahod**.
 
• **Gujarat** led the national tally in the implementation of the **11 critical interventions**, particularly in ensuring **100 percent** registration for **Ayushman Bharat cards** and **PM-Kisan** benefits among its five identified PVTG communities: **Sidi**, **Padhar**, **Kathodi**, **Kotwalia**, and **Kolgha**.
 
• The **Ministry of Tribal Affairs** recognized the state's progress in utilizing **GIS mapping** for tribal habitations, which facilitated the rapid approval of **pucca houses** under **PM-Awas Yojana (Gramin)** and the extension of **off-grid solar power** to remote areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **PM-JANMAN Scheme Framework**:

 
 
• The scheme has a total financial outlay of **24,104 crore**, with a central share of **15,336 crore** and a state share of **8,768 crore**.
 
• It focuses on **11 key interventions** coordinated by **9 Central Ministries**, including the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare**, **Ministry of Power**, and **Ministry of Rural Development**.
 
• The mission aims to bridge gaps in **safe housing**, **clean drinking water**, **sanitation**, and **telecommunication connectivity** for approximately **28 lakh** PVTG individuals living in **22,000 habitations** across **18 states and one UT**.
 
• Infrastructural targets include the construction of **8,000 km of all-weather roads** and the setting up of **2,500 Anganwadi centres** and **Multipurpose Centres (MPCs)**.

questions.question: Which institution developed the Sabal 20, an electric unmanned helicopter acquired by the Indian Army in November 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**IIT Kanpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sabal 20** is a sophisticated **Electric Unmanned Helicopter** designed specifically for heavy-lift logistics and reconnaissance in challenging terrains.
 
• This cutting-edge technology was developed by **EndureAir Systems**, a deep-tech startup incubated at the **Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kanpur**.
 
• The **Indian Army** officially inducted the **Sabal 20** in **November 2024** to enhance its logistics capabilities in high-altitude sectors such as **Ladakh** and **Sikkim**.
 
• It features a **Vertical Take-Off and Landing (VTOL)** capability, which allows it to operate effectively in restricted spaces without the need for a runway.
 
• The helicopter is designed to carry payloads of up to **20 kilograms** and can operate at altitudes exceeding **15,000 feet**, providing a critical advantage in mountainous warfare.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **EndureAir Systems**:

 
 
• Founded by researchers and alumni from the **Aerospace Engineering** department of **IIT Kanpur** under the mentorship of Professor **Abhishek**.
 
• The startup focuses on providing indigenous **unmanned aerial solutions** for both defense and civilian applications, aligning with the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative.
 
 
 
• **Operational Features**:
 
 
• The **electric propulsion** system ensures a significantly lower **acoustic signature** compared to traditional combustion engines, making it ideal for covert operations.
 
• It is equipped with advanced **autonomous navigation** systems, allowing it to perform **last-mile delivery** of medicines and essential supplies to remote forward posts.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Significance**:
 
 
• Reduces the reliance on **animal transport** or large manned helicopters (like the Cheetah or Dhruv) for small-scale logistics, thereby saving operational costs and reducing risk to human pilots.
 
• Supports the **Indian Army** in maintaining a constant supply chain in **low-oxygen** and **high-wind** environments where traditional drones often fail.

questions.question: As announced in January 2025, which organization developed indigenously produced 'Paracetamol'?

options.text: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
All India Institute of Medical Sciences
Jubilee Mission Medical College and Research Institute

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Council of Scientific and Industrial Research**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)**, specifically through the **Indian Institute of Chemical Technology (IICT)** based in **Hyderabad**, announced the successful development of a fully indigenous technology for **Paracetamol** production in **January 2025**.
 
• The project focused on synthesizing the **Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API)** using locally sourced raw materials, effectively reducing the heavy reliance on imported **Key Starting Materials (KSMs)** like **Para-Aminophenol**.
 
• This development is a critical milestone under the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative, which seeks to secure India s medical supply chain and achieve self-sufficiency in essential drug manufacturing.
 
• The newly developed process is designed to be **environmentally sustainable** and **cost-competitive**, allowing domestic manufacturers to produce high-quality **analgesics** and **antipyretics** for both local consumption and global export.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)**:

 
 
• Established in **September 1942**, it is India s premier public sector **Research and Development** organization.
 
• It operates under the **Ministry of Science and Technology** and is presided over by the **Prime Minister of India**.
 
• With a network of **37 national laboratories**, it plays a pivotal role in fields such as **genomics**, **oceanography**, and **pharmaceutical chemistry**.
 
 
 
• **Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs)**:
 
 
• An **API** is the primary chemical component in a drug responsible for the therapeutic effect.
 
• To boost domestic production, the Indian government introduced the **Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme** for **Bulk Drugs** and promoted the establishment of **Bulk Drug Parks**.
 
• Reducing **import dependency** (specifically from **China**) for **APIs** is a strategic priority to prevent medicine shortages.

questions.question:
Which of the following is NOT a relay event in track events in sports? 

I. 4×100 metres

II. 4×600 metres
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **4×100 metres relay** is a standard track and field sprint event where four runners each complete a distance of **100 metres** in succession. This event is a primary discipline in the **Summer Olympic Games** and **World Athletics Championships**, requiring athletes to pass a **baton** within a **30-metre exchange zone**. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• The **4×600 metres** is not a recognized or standard international relay event in competitive athletics. Standard middle-distance relays sanctioned by **World Athletics** (formerly **IAAF**) include the **4×400 metres**, **4×800 metres**, and **4×1500 metres**, but the 600m distance is not utilized for major championship relay formats. ***Hence, statement II is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Relay Race Mechanics**:

 
 
• **Baton Passing**: In short relays like the **4×100m**, runners typically use a **non-visual exchange** (blind handoff) to maintain top speed, while longer relays may use a **visual exchange**.
 
• **Legs**: A relay team consists of a **lead-off leg**, two middle runners, and an **anchor leg** (usually the fastest runner).
 
• **Exchange Zone**: For the **4×100m**, the current **World Athletics** rules define a single **30-metre** zone where the **baton** must be handed over; failing to do so results in disqualification.
 
 
 
• **Standard Track Events**:
 
 
• **4×400 metres**: Often the finale of track meets, involving one full lap per runner.
 
• **Mixed 4×400 metres Relay**: A modern event featuring two men and two women, which made its **Olympic debut** at the **Tokyo 2020 Games**.
 
• **Medley Relays**: These involve legs of different distances (e.g., **1200m**, **400m**, **800m**, **1600m** in the **Distance Medley Relay**).

questions.question: According to Fleming left hand rule, which of the following is denoted using the second finger of the left hand?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Direction of current**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fleming's Left-Hand Rule** is a simple visualization tool used to find the direction of the **mechanical force** (motion) experienced by a **current-carrying conductor** when it is placed in an external **magnetic field**.
 
• To apply the rule, the **thumb**, **forefinger** (first finger), and **middle finger** (second finger) of the **left hand** are held mutually **perpendicular** (at 90 degrees) to one another.
 
• The **Forefinger** (First finger) represents the direction of the **Magnetic Field** (B), typically pointing from the **North pole** to the **South pole**.
 
• The **Middle Finger** (Second finger) represents the direction of the **Electric Current** (I) flowing through the conductor.
 
• The **Thumb** represents the direction of the **Thrust** or **Force** (F) acting on the conductor, which dictates its direction of **motion**.
 
• This rule is essentially a mnemonic for the **Lorentz Force** equation, where the force vector is the cross-product of the current and magnetic field vectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Direction of magnetic field**

 
 
• In the left-hand rule, this is indicated by the **index finger**.
 
• In **SI units**, the strength of this field is measured in **Tesla** (T).
 
 
 
• **Force acting on the conductor**
 
 
• This is represented by the **thumb**.
 
• The magnitude of this force is given by the formula **F = B × I × L × sin(θ)**, where **L** is the length of the wire and **θ** is the angle between the current and the field.
 
 
 
• **Measure of resistance**
 
 
• **Resistance** is a property of a material to oppose the flow of current, defined by **Ohm's Law** (R = V / I).
 
• It is not determined or represented by **Fleming's rules**, which deal with **electromagnetism** and **motion** rather than circuit properties.
 
 
 
• **Electric Motors**
 
 
• Fleming's Left-Hand Rule is the fundamental principle used to understand the operation of **DC Motors**, where electrical energy is converted into **mechanical torque**.

questions.question: Who is the composer of treatise of music Swaramelakalanidhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ramamatya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The treatise **Swaramelakalanidhi** was composed by the scholar-musician **Ramamatya** in approximately **1550 AD**.
 
• **Ramamatya** served as a prominent minister and court musician under **Aliya Rama Raya**, the de facto ruler of the **Vijayanagara Empire**.
 
• This work is historically significant as it marks the formal beginning of the **Carnatic music** system, acting as a bridge between the ancient traditions and modern practices.
 
• In **Swaramelakalanidhi**, the author introduced the **Mela** system of classification, identifying **20 Melas** (parent scales) to organize various **Ragas** of that era.
 
• The text provides a detailed study of **Veena** construction and tuning, categorizing them into types like **Shuddha Mela Veena** and **Madhya Mela Veena**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Matanga**:

 
 
• Author of the influential text **Brihaddeshi**, dated between the **6th and 8th centuries**.
 
• He was the first to technically define the term **Raga** and introduced the **Desi** (regional) music tradition.
 
 
 
• **Sharngadeva**:
 
 
• Composed the **Sangeeta Ratnakara** in the **13th century** during the **Yadava dynasty** in **Devagiri**.
 
• His work is known as **Saptadhyayi** (consisting of seven chapters) and is a foundational text for both **Hindustani** and **Carnatic** music.
 
 
 
• **Haripala**:
 
 
• A **Chalukyan king** credited with writing **Sangeeta Sudhakara** in the **12th or 14th century**.
 
• He is recognized for being one of the earliest theorists to explicitly differentiate between **Hindustani** and **Carnatic** musical styles.

questions.question: Magnetite is the finest iron ore with a very high content of iron up to ___ per cent.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**70**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Magnetite** is the most superior and **finest iron ore** found in the Earth's crust, distinguished by its high metallic iron concentration, which can reach up to **70%**.
 
• Chemically, it is a ferrimagnetic mineral represented by the formula **Fe₃O₄**, making it the most **magnetic** of all the naturally occurring minerals on Earth.
 
• Due to these excellent **magnetic qualities**, **Magnetite** is of immense value in the **electrical industry**, where it is utilized in the production of specialized components and high-efficiency motors.
 
• The ore typically appears **black or brownish-black** with a metallic luster and is primarily found in **igneous and metamorphic rocks**, as well as in **banded iron formations (BIFs)**.
 
• In **India**, high-grade **Magnetite** deposits are concentrated in the **Kudremukh** mines of **Karnataka**, which are known to be one of the largest deposits of this type in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hematite (Fe₂O₃)**:

 
 
• It is often referred to as 'red ore' and contains a slightly lower iron content ranging from **50% to 60%**.
 
• Despite having a lower iron percentage than magnetite, it is the most important **industrial iron ore** in terms of the total quantity used in **iron and steel manufacturing**.
 
 
 
• **Limonite and Siderite**:
 
 
• **Limonite** is a secondary iron ore with a content of **40% to 60%**, often appearing yellowish in color.
 
• **Siderite** is an iron carbonate (FeCO₃) containing less than **40%** iron, making it less economically desirable for extraction.
 
 
 
• **Geographic Distribution**:
 
 
• The major iron ore belts in India include the **Odisha-Jharkhand belt**, the **Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt**, and the **Bellary-Chitradurga-Chikkamagaluru-Tumakuru belt**.
 
• While **Hematite** is predominantly found in **Odisha** and **Chhattisgarh**, **Magnetite** is largely exported from the **Mangaluru port**.
